questions.q: SELECT StageName, COUNT(Id) FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName returns what?
options: One row per individual opportunity record
A single row summarizing all opportunities regardless of stage
One summary row per distinct StageName value
An error, because COUNT() cannot be combined with GROUP BY
questions.explain: GROUP BY produces one row per distinct value of the grouped field, each with its own aggregate — not one overall summary and not one row per record.

questions.q: What rule governs selecting a plain (non-aggregated) field alongside an aggregate function?
options: The plain field is automatically aggregated using MAX()
Plain fields cannot be combined with aggregate functions in the same query
The plain field must be wrapped in COUNT_DISTINCT()
The plain field must also appear in the GROUP BY list
questions.explain: Any selected field that isn't inside an aggregate function must appear in GROUP BY, otherwise SOQL has no defined value to show for it within a multi-row group.

questions.q: What is the key difference between WHERE and HAVING in a query that uses GROUP BY?
options: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
WHERE and HAVING are interchangeable in SOQL
HAVING filters rows before grouping; WHERE filters after aggregation
WHERE can only be used with aggregate functions, HAVING cannot
questions.explain: WHERE operates before aggregation on individual rows; HAVING operates after aggregation, filtering based on the aggregate value itself.

questions.q: Why can't WHERE COUNT(Id) > 5 be used to express 'only stages with more than 5 opportunities'?
options: WHERE cannot contain any numeric comparison
WHERE is evaluated before aggregation happens, so it has no aggregated value to reference yet
COUNT(Id) is not a valid aggregate function in SOQL
WHERE can only reference the GROUP BY field itself
questions.explain: Aggregation hasn't occurred yet at the point WHERE is evaluated, so an aggregate condition like COUNT(Id) > 5 belongs in HAVING instead.

questions.q: SELECT StageName, LeadSource, COUNT(Id) FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName, LeadSource produces one row per:
options: Unique LeadSource only, ignoring StageName
Unique StageName only, with LeadSource values mixed arbitrarily
Unique combination of StageName and LeadSource
Individual Opportunity record
questions.explain: Grouping by two fields together produces one row per unique combination of both fields' values, not per either field alone.
